title: Locally Scrambled Quantum Memories for Loss-Tolerant Entanglement-Assisted Optical Interferometry
abstract: We formulate a loss-tolerant extension of entanglement-assisted long-baseline optical interferometry in which the astronomical optical coherence is first mapped coherently to distributed quantum memories and is subsequently protected by local scrambling encoders. The proposal must be distinguished from existing memory-assisted Gottesman--Jennewein--Croke (GJC) interferometers, in which quantum memories store an ancillary single-photon-entangled reference rather than the astronomical state itself. We derive the weak-thermal-light model, its two-parameter quantum Fisher information (QFI) matrix, the GJC measurement probabilities, and the associated classical Fisher information (CFI). We then prove that exact local correction of flagged erasures restores the complete complex visibility, its QFI matrix, and the operational GJC CFI. The relevant protection criterion is reference--environment decoupling, not volume-law entanglement alone. We state, as conjectures, quantitative decoupling bounds for local random encoders and finite-depth scramblers, and derive the expected threshold of fewer than one half of the physical memories erased per node. Finally, we formulate the phase-covariance and superselection-rule constraints required for a physically meaningful distributed protocol.
summary: This paper proposes a robust method for long-baseline optical interferometry using distributed quantum memories. It introduces local scrambling encoders that protect the stored astronomical coherence against photon loss and erasure. The key finding is that under specific conditions of exact local correction, the measurement's sensitivity (quantified by QFI) is fully preserved, enabling practical quantum sensing in noisy channels.
main_problem: To develop a loss-tolerant protocol for long-baseline optical interferometry by mapping astronomical coherence into quantum memories protected by local scrambling encoders.
main_result: The authors prove that exact local erasure correction restores the complex visibility, Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and operational GJC Fisher Information (CFI) of the stored state.
method: Theoretical derivation involving modeling weak-thermal-light sources, applying concepts of quantum channel preservation under recovery operations, and establishing necessary decoupling criteria.
model_or_system: The system models a distributed network connecting two telescopes using quantum memories to store the astronomical optical coherence. The process involves coherent signal storage followed by local scrambling encoding and erasure correction.
key_observables: Complex visibility ($g$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) matrix, Classical Fisher Information (CFI), and the Decoupling Error ($	ext{DE}(V)$).
important_parameters: The critical threshold for successful recovery is established as fewer than half of the physical memories erased per node ($k/n < 1/2$).
main_assumptions: The protocol relies on assuming exact local erasure correction and that protection is governed by reference–environment decoupling rather than just volume-law entanglement.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the weak-thermal-light model, establishing the QFI/CFI diagnostics for GJC readout, proving the restoration of coherence and Fisher information under local recovery operations (Theorem 1 & 2), and finally outlining necessary constraints like U(1) covariance.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum communication challenges in noisy environments by providing rigorous mathematical guarantees (QFI preservation) for resource-limited quantum measurements, which is highly relevant to quantum networking and sensing.
